shared_elements: bird in profile with prominent hooked/pointed beak
animal or human heads shown frontally in a row
stacked vertical registers on a tall stone monument
horizontal band of repeating pattern separating registers
limbs and clawed feet rendered schematically
justification: Both are tall vertical stone monuments organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a row of frontal heads or a dominant bird at the top, a band of repeating pattern acting as a divider, and profile creatures including beaked birds below. The decisive difference is the mode of carving and rendering: A is a fully three-dimensional, tightly interlocking sculpture in the round (drawn in ink, with crossed arms and mirrored birds), while B is a shallow, loosely spaced low relief on a flat slab whose animals are scattered rather than interlocked.
